name: NIF — one shot from master oscillator to target
description:
A pulsed master laser is split through a beamsplitter cascade into eleven equal-power ports, each with its own delay line, EOM, and amplifier proxy, timed so all eleven pulses arrive on one target within a fraction of a nanosecond of each other — loosely inspired by the National Ignition Facility's beam architecture.

Caution: this is a schematic illustration, not an accurate model of a real NIF shot — the amplifier stages in particular are simplified passive proxies, not a real gain chain. The real facility (see lasers.llnl.gov, and specifically lasers.llnl.gov/lighting-beam-path) amplifies its laser light more than 10 billion times, splits it into 192 individual beams rather than eleven, converts each beam's wavelength from infrared to ultraviolet in transport, and converges them with pinpoint accuracy on a hohlraum target inside the Target Chamber at up to millions of joules and hundreds of terawatts — culminating in the December 2022 shot that produced more fusion energy (3.15 MJ) than the 2.05 MJ of laser energy that drove it. This setup only illustrates the timing-and-convergence geometry, nothing more.

params.text: One master laser source → 11 causally connected representative quad ports → one absorbing target surrogate
Zoom and pan to inspect split ratios, fibers, timing trim, passive amplifier proxies, final optics, and target.
Reality scale: NIF has 48 chamber beam ports, four beams per port (192 beamlines). This readable 2D slice displays 11 live representative ports.
Sequential splits make eleven equal-power displayed seeds. This stands in for NIF’s PAM beam shaping and four-way PABTS distribution.
Each port is active: fiber seed → collimator → timing trim → EOM/PEPC proxy → passive glass slab → 2ω → 3ω → focus.
The 11-way radial layout is a readable 2D projection, not NIF’s literal four 3D cone angles. Every P01–P11 path is traced from the same source.
target element is real absorption; hohlraum x-ray conversion, capsule implosion, fusion, and yield are not modeled
DANTE: x-ray power history · annotation only (no x-ray transport)
nTOF: neutron time of flight · annotation only (no neutron transport)
VISAR: shock-velocity diagnostic · annotation only (no coherent interference or velocity inference)
Simulated: geometric paths, bounded relative signal, wavelengths, polarization, pulsed timing, fiber delay, detector arrivals.
Constructed from existing optics only: laser, BS, fiber, lens, delay, EOM, freeform glass, crystals, sample, detector.
Not simulated: gain/saturation, flashlamps, four-pass amplifier switching, damage, diffraction/phase, 3D cones, x rays, implosion, fusion, neutrons.
